subject: MedSys pilot: coordination for dedicated GPU slice + autoscale exception
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Park <emily.park@medsys.ai>
Cc: Dr. Alan Chen <a.chen@medsys.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MedSys pilot: dedicated GPU slice request + nightly sweep exception

Emily / Alan —

Thanks again for agreeing to run the prototype with us. To make the upcoming week of model validation smooth on our side, we wanted to propose a short-term dedicated allocation and an autoscale exception for scheduled nightly sensitivity sweeps. High-level ask:

- Temporary reserved slice: 4x A100-equivalent GPUs (us-west) for 6 weeks starting Aug 4
- Autoscale exception: allow scheduled overnight batch runs (00:00–04:00 PT) to burst beyond normal headroom up to the reserved slice for nightly sweep jobs only
- Canary policy: we will run canaries the first 48 hours and revert to public-hosted variant if latency or errors spike

Model/traffic details (summary):
- Model: medbert-v2 (70B float16 -> quantized int8 in prod), checkpoint v2.1
- Expected steady-state qps: 2–5 for interactive calls; nightly sweep throughput: ~1.8M tokens over 3.5 hours
- Latency SLO target: p95 < 300ms for interactive flows

I attached the pilot SLA draft and a one-page resource plan. Could you confirm: (1) procurement timeline for signatures, (2) any data residency constraints we need to account for, and (3) acceptance of the canary/rollback plan outlined on p2 of the SLA?

If this is acceptable, I’ll loop in Product and Ops to finalize the reservation window and get the temporary quota pushed.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.ai
Attachments: pilot-sla-proposal.pdf, resource-plan.xlsx
From: Emily Park <emily.park@medsys.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@medsys.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jul 2025 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MedSys pilot: dedicated GPU slice request + nightly sweep exception

Thanks Rafael — this looks helpful. A few initial items from our side:

- Procurement: I looped Procurement to get an initial read; we can sign an amendment but need cost line items by Tuesday EOD so we can slot the approval meeting on Wed.
- Data residency: MedSys requires that PHI-related inference only stays in the US. We plan to anonymize upstream, but can you confirm logs/audit retention settings for the pilot?
- Fallbacks: Can you confirm what happens if the reserved slice is unavailable (e.g., a hardware issue) during an overnight sweep? Is there an automated fallback to a compatible hosted instance and what are the latency expectations?

Also copying Dr. Alan for clinical validation items — Alan, any concerns about the nightly sweep cadence?

Emily Park
Head of AI Partnerships, MedSys Health
emily.park@medsys.ai

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emily Park <emily.park@medsys.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Jul 2025 09:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MedSys pilot: dedicated GPU slice request + nightly sweep exception

Rafael / team —

Quick product/ops questions so we can scope the reservation correctly before committing:

1) Model runtime variant: do you expect medbert-v2 to run quantized (int8) in the reserved pool from day one, or will it arrive float16 and be converted during the pilot? If quantization is planned, we should confirm kernel compatibility and memory footprint.

2) Canary cadence and rollout gating: we need explicit success criteria for the 48h canary (error rate threshold, p95 latency threshold, and a fuzz test against our input set). Please add those criteria to the resource-plan.xlsx (I can add a template).

3) Autoscale exception scope: Ops prefers to limit exceptions to scheduled cron jobs tied to a job id namespace (e.g., ms-pilot-nightly/*). That way we can enforce that interactive traffic never consumes the burst. Is that acceptable?

4) Fallback behavior: If the reserved slice becomes unhealthy, we will trigger automatic routing to the closest compatible hosted variant with a rate-limited queue; interactive latency may increase but we should guarantee functional continuity. We need MedSys to acknowledge the fallback and sign the amendment calling out degraded latency SLAs during failover windows.

Laura / Marcus — can you estimate the lead time to provision a 4-GPU dedicated slice in us-west and whether we can support a hard carveout on Aug 4 if Procurement signs by Aug 1?

Kimberly Park
Product Lead, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.ai

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Park <emily.park@medsys.ai>, Procurement <procurement@medsys.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 23 Jul 2025 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MedSys pilot: dedicated GPU slice request + nightly sweep exception — agreed next steps

Team — thanks for the quick responses. Short summary and next steps so everyone has a single source of truth: 

1) Reservation: Ops (Laura / Marcus) confirmed they can provision a 4x GPU dedicated slice in us-west and tentatively hold Aug 4–Sep 15 for MedSys, conditional on Procurement signature by Aug 1.

2) Autoscale exception: Approved for scheduled nightly sweep jobs only. Scope limited to job namespace ms-pilot-nightly/* and time window 00:00–04:00 PT. Interactive traffic is explicitly excluded.

3) Canary and rollback: Kimberly will add explicit success criteria to resource-plan.xlsx (error rate < 1.5%, p95 < 300ms, end-to-end smoke tests pass). If canary fails, traffic will be diverted to a hosted compatible variant and we will pause gardened sweep runs.

4) Data residency & audit logs: Logs containing any PHI will remain within US regions. Tech Ops will set retention to 90 days for pilot audit logs; longer retention can be negotiated in the full contract.

5) Fallback SLA: We will provide an amendment describing degraded latency expectations during failover (p95 up to 900ms) and DocuSign link is attached for signature (amendment-docusign-link.txt).

Immediate asks: Rafael -> Emily/Procurement: confirm cost OK and signature timeline (deadline Aug 1).
Laura/Marcus -> Rafael/Kimberly: confirm final provisioning ETA and the runbook for slice health checks (Jira INF-2331).
Kimberly -> Rafael: add the canary success criteria to resource-plan.xlsx and share the updated file by EOD tomorrow.

I’ve attached the updated resource plan with minor edits and the DocuSign link. If all good, I’ll formally request the quota carveout and route the amendment.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.ai
Attachments: resource-plan.xlsx, amendment-docusign-link.txt
